explanations.answer: Very much of the land remains to be possessed
explanations.explanation: That's exactly what the LORD says. "You are old and well along in years, but very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) Joshua, Israel's leader, has done a LOT, and there's still a lot left. I know that feeling, friend. You finish one tray and the counter is still covered.

explanations.answer: All of the land has now been possessed
explanations.explanation: I see why that sounds nice, friend. But the LORD says the opposite: "…very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) Joshua, Israel's leader, is old and well along in years, and there's still plenty left to take. Picture opening the oven door, ready to call it a day, and finding three more batches of dough waiting for you.

explanations.answer: The land must wait for a new leader
explanations.explanation: Joshua is old, so that's a fair guess. But the LORD doesn't mention a new leader here. He talks to Joshua about the land and says, "…very much of the land remains to be possessed." (Joshua 13:1) The job is still sitting on Joshua's counter.

Yes, baker! The LORD says, "…I Myself will drive out before the Israelites." (Joshua 13:6) That covers all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians. He puts Himself right in that sentence as the One who drives them out. Then He gives Joshua a different job: divide the land by lot.

Joshua is Israel's leader, so he's a natural guess. But look at who the LORD names here: "…I Myself will drive out before the Israelites." (Joshua 13:6) He puts Himself right in that sentence. Joshua's job in the verse is to divide the land by lot.

explanations.answer: The tribes east of the Jordan
explanations.explanation: Those tribes already have their land from Moses, so they're a tempting pick. But the LORD doesn't hand this job to them. He says, "…I Myself will drive out before the Israelites." (Joshua 13:6) The answer is right there in the first words of that promise.

True! The LORD says, "Be sure to divide it by lot as an inheritance to Israel, as I have commanded you." (Joshua 13:6) Even with land still to be taken, He wants it divided. That tells me He's serious about what He promised.

This one is true, friend. The LORD says, "Be sure to divide it by lot as an inheritance to Israel, as I have commanded you." (Joshua 13:6) The land isn't all taken yet, and He still tells Joshua to divide it. I like that you were careful, though.

explanations.answer: Nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh
explanations.explanation: That's it! The LORD says, "Now therefore divide this land as an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) So this land is for nine tribes plus half of Manasseh. The other half of Manasseh had already received its inheritance from Moses beyond the Jordan (Joshua 13:8). Keep an eye on that half, friend.

Twelve tribes is the number everybody remembers. But the LORD says this land goes "…to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) The other half of Manasseh, along with the Reubenites and Gadites, had already received the inheritance Moses gave them beyond the Jordan (Joshua 13:8). So they weren't waiting on this land.

explanations.answer: The tribes of Reuben and Gad
explanations.explanation: Reuben and Gad are a fair guess, since they do come up in this chapter. But they had already received their inheritance from Moses beyond the Jordan (Joshua 13:8). This land is for "…the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh." (Joshua 13:7) Their batch was already baked, boxed and sealed.

I see why you'd say that, since the east was Moses' conquest. But the text says, "…the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites." (Joshua 13:13) So the answer is false. And it adds that Geshur and Maacath "…dwell among the Israelites to this day."

False is right, baker! The text says, "…the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. So Geshur and Maacath dwell among the Israelites to this day." (Joshua 13:13) Just before that, Moses, Israel's leader, had struck down Og's kingdom and dispossessed them (Joshua 13:12). Then this verse turns and says these two peoples were not driven out. I think that's a detail worth holding onto.

explanations.answer: The food offerings to the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker! Levi is the tribe set apart to carry the ark and serve the LORD (Deuteronomy 10:8), and Moses gave them no land. Their inheritance is this: "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) A few verses later it's said again: "The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:33) Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh got territory from Moses, and Levi got a promise instead. I think that's worth a second look.

Gold sounds like a nice inheritance, but this passage doesn't give it to Levi. It says, "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) That's the inheritance the verse names for them. Moses gave them no land.

Sihon's cities are real, but they went to Reuben and Gad (Joshua 13:21, 27). Levi gets something different: "The food offerings to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, just as He had promised them." (Joshua 13:14) Sihon, king of the Amorites, is not on Levi's list.
